title: iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS: Screen and controls
lead: Use the running Apple app to choose a source, change playback settings, compare controls and inspect applied code. Follow operations with SDK state and events. iPhone/iPad and tvOS differences are explained beside the relevant steps.

items.label: Implementation guide: PlayerConfig, source configuration, UI changes and FAQ

blocks.text: Preparation and build
Build and launch Showcase-iOS or Showcase-tvOS using Local setup and licenses. This chapter starts with the running app; Swift integration and UI source changes are in the implementation guide.

The app uses Player 3.128.0, with iOS/iPadOS 16.0 or later and tvOS 15.0 or later. Allow com.playerlab.ios or com.playerlab.tvos on the Player license for the target you run. A successful build alone does not confirm authentication or playback.
Suggested screen workflow

The video sits above a scrollable control panel. Source selects a preset; Configuration opens settings; Public SDK APIs opens the API, playlist and supported feature panels. Playback tracks reports current selections and position. iPhone/iPad uses sheets; tvOS uses full-screen forms, remote focus, Select and the system keyboard.

blocks.caption: The iPad screen after an applied track selection. The video, Playback tracks and configuration entry show where to begin. The German subtitle belongs to this recorded example.

items: Select VOD HLS under Source and start playback with the player's Play button. Autoplay is off and mute is on at startup. Confirm that the picture and timeline advance before changing settings.

Open Configure source and playback. For a first comparison, keep the source URL, enter 5 for Start offset and choose Start. Apply should report Reload source. Start playback if needed and check that it begins near the requested position; the SDK can correct positions to media boundaries.

Reopen the editor. From startup defaults, turn Autoplay from off to on while keeping Start muted on. Check Recreate player and reload source, then Apply. Compare automatic muted startup. Only a changed player setting recreates the player; unchanged values disable Apply.
On iOS or iPadOS, select Default, Sports, Live (DVR), or Cinema under Player UI to compare controls and layouts. Switching UI reloads playback. tvOS uses System UI and has no Web UI selector.
For audio and subtitle selection or video scaling, follow the settings below using a source that contains the required tracks. Playback tracks shows the current native selections.

Open Show applied code in Configuration and compare the applied values with your change. Then use API inspector → Operations, State and Events to run a command and check its result, following the detailed steps below.

To try live rewind, select Live HLS, start playback and wait for a rewind window. The negative helper offsets are distances behind the live edge. Use Go to live edge to return, then check behindLive, atLiveEdge and the event log.

blocks.text: Changing the iOS UI recreates the Player and SwiftUI view and reloads the selected source. It does not preserve playback position or playing state. Compare appearances with that reload behavior in mind. The Sports scores and player details are fictional sample data, not a sports-data service.

blocks.title: Do not add DASH to the Apple catalog
blocks.text: The Apple SDK in this configuration accepts HLS and progressive MP4. The app’s catalog contains only HLS. Loading DASH with the pinned SDK causes a precondition failure and terminates the app. Do not add it to the catalog even though SourceKind includes a DASH enum case. Use Web or Android to compare DASH behavior.

blocks.caption: A tvOS screen from the recorded remote-input test. Use Play/Pause on the remote and move focus to configuration. This screenshot does not establish behavior on every physical device.

blocks.text: Edit source and playback configuration

items: Choose Configure source and playback below the source presets. iPhone and iPad show a sheet; tvOS opens a full-screen native form. On tvOS, move focus with the remote and press Select; text fields use the system keyboard.

Enter an absolute HTTP(S) Source URL, choose HLS or Progressive MP4, and optionally enter a title and HTTP(S) poster URL. Empty title or poster fields clear them. Cached HLS uses the separate offline inspector; DASH is not supported.

Set an optional start offset in seconds and choose Automatic, Start, or End. Blank offset uses the SDK default. Automatic means the beginning for VOD and the live edge for live. Signed finite offsets are accepted and the SDK corrects them to stream boundaries; live offsets apply when playback starts.

Choose Autoplay after source load, Start muted, and SDK time shift / DVR. Defaults are off, on, and on. The separate Allow DVR controls (app) switch also governs the app quick-seek buttons. Enter maximum bitrate in whole bit/s (0 = unlimited) and forward buffer in finite nonnegative seconds (0 = SDK choice).

Read Reload source or Recreate player and reload source before selecting Apply. Invalid fields show an explanation and disable Apply. Reset to applied restores only the draft; Cancel discards it. Applied settings last for the current app session.

blocks.text: Source fields, start position and initial track preferences reload the source on the existing player. Playback, scaling, bitrate and buffer changes recreate the player and native view, then reload the complete source including title, poster and offset options. UI mode, the app DVR switch and event log remain in place. Apply restarts at the configured offset according to Autoplay. Selecting a source preset resets its source fields and initial track preferences while retaining player settings.

rows: Source
Title: Player Lab VOD; keep the selected HLS URL
Reloads the source. Check SourceConfig.title in Show applied code. A title alone does not change the media or its tracks.
Start position
Start offset: 5; Offset reference: Start
Reloads the source. Start playback and compare the first position with the beginning of the VOD. Blank offset restores the SDK default; use End with a negative offset for a live source.
Playback
Autoplay: off → on; Start muted: on
From startup defaults, turn Autoplay on and Apply. A changed player setting recreates the player. Check automatic muted playback; unchanged values disable Apply.
Initial tracks
Audio language: de-AT; Initial subtitles: Preferred language; subtitle language: de
Reloads the source. On a source with matching renditions, check Playback tracks and visible captions after initial Ready. An unavailable preference keeps the default selection.
Video scaling
Fill (crop), then Fit
Recreates the player. Use a display area with a different aspect ratio from the video to see cropping versus the full picture.
Adaptation and buffer
Maximum bitrate: 1500000 bit/s; Forward buffer: 10 seconds

Recreates the player. Check adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate and bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration in applied code. These are configuration limits/targets; the actual quality and buffered media depend on the source and playback.

blocks.text: To return to the initial player defaults, enter Autoplay off, Start muted on, SDK time shift / DVR on, Maximum bitrate 0, Forward buffer 0 and Video scaling Fit, then Apply. Reset to applied only abandons draft edits; it does not restore defaults. Selecting VOD HLS again clears custom source fields and initial track preferences while keeping player settings. Applied configuration is kept for the current app session.

blocks.title: Apply and reset
blocks.text: No configuration changes means the draft matches the applied values and Apply is disabled. Reset to applied restores those applied values in the draft; Cancel discards edits. Neither changes current playback.

items: After Apply, open Show applied code and inspect active Player, Source and UI values.
Edit a draft without applying and confirm the output stays unchanged. iPhone/iPad supports Copy code and text selection; tvOS provides focusable code lines without clipboard integration.

blocks.caption: Applied Swift configuration on iPad. The export shows scaling and source options, excludes drafts and uses a Player key placeholder.
Applied Swift configuration on tvOS. Focusable wrapped lines support remote reading; this TV host has no clipboard integration.

blocks.text: Additional SDK settings

items: Open Configure source and playback and enable Edit additional Player, Source and view settings under Advanced SDK settings. Search Filter configuration API name for a property.

Enable its Override. The input provides a switch, SDK enumeration, value field, structured JSON or callback body according to the property's type. Read its accepted values and units. Disabling the override restores the basic form value or SDK default.

Check the pending action and Apply. Source settings reload the source; Player and view settings recreate the player. Invalid values leave active settings unchanged. Show applied code displays the Swift configuration from the applied values.
In API inspector → State, select Refresh SDK state to check the loaded source, tracks or player value. An option may affect playback only with matching content, a service or a supported device.

blocks.text: Structured fields create the public SDK objects described below the input. SourceConfig.tracks accepts an array of subtitle objects with unique identifiers. An empty array clears additional tracks; disabling its override removes the explicit setting.

blocks.caption: SourceConfig.tracks in the iPhone editor. Each object describes a subtitle track, with accepted properties listed below the input.

blocks.text: This adds a manual track without a remote file or subtitle cues. After Apply, inspect Player.availableSubtitles, then use the subtitle and cue operations to supply and select cues. For a file, provide its HTTP(S) URL and format, such as webVtt. External subtitle rendering depends on the selected UI; native HLS subtitle renditions remain the common route for tvOS System UI.

blocks.caption: Player.availableSubtitles after Apply includes manual-example alongside the source's native tracks.

blocks.text: To undo an applied setting, disable its Override and Apply. Reset to applied only abandons draft edits; it does not remove an override that is already active. A setting may need matching media, a supported device or an external service before it has a visible effect.
Editable callbacks

items: Search for a callback such as LabelingConfig.audioLabel and enable its override. Read the description of input and the required return type.
Enter a function body, such as return 'GUI ' + input.label; for this label callback, then Apply. Editing the draft alone does not install or invoke it.
Use content that causes the SDK to call the function. In API inspector → State, filter Callback and refresh. Calls and failures distinguish an installed function from one actually invoked by the SDK.
Inspect Show applied code. To restore the SDK behavior, disable the override and Apply.

blocks.caption: The audio-label callback accepts a JavaScript body that returns a replacement for the label in input.
State after the SDK invoked the applied audio-label body. Counts are shown without callback payloads.

blocks.title: Execution and fallback
blocks.text: Callbacks use a bounded plain-value interpreter. Invalid syntax prevents Apply; execution errors or an invalid result use the documented fallback. Stage and Apply do not prove a callback ran: trigger its SDK path and inspect calls/failures. Disable the Override and Apply to restore behavior. The implementation guide describes supported syntax and reuse.
Initial tracks and video scaling

items: Use a source with native HLS audio/subtitle renditions. In Initial tracks, enter an optional audio language such as de-AT and choose Automatic, Off or Preferred language for subtitles. Enter a subtitle language only for Preferred language.

Blank audio and Automatic subtitles keep the SDK/OS choice. A full language tag matches first, then its primary language; de-AT can select de. An unavailable language leaves the default in place. Off calls the SDK subtitle-selection API with nil.

Choose Fit, Fill (crop) or Stretch. Fit preserves aspect ratio inside the view; Fill preserves it and crops the edges; Stretch fills the view without preserving it. Check the pending action, then Apply. Reset changes only the draft.

blocks.caption: Initial track preferences in the iPad form. These are source-local application preferences, applied once at initial Ready, rather than PlayerConfig language properties.
Preferred subtitle language and Fill (crop). Scaling is the SDK StyleConfig.scalingMode setting and recreates the player.

blocks.text: The language fields use the public availableAudio/availableSubtitles and setAudio/setSubtitle APIs after the intended Source loads and reaches its first Ready. They are application preferences, not additional PlayerConfig fields. Later choices in the SDK track menu remain until the next source load. Scaling is a separate creation-time SDK field, StyleConfig.scalingMode.

blocks.title: Why selection waits for Ready
blocks.text: In the checked Player 3.128.0 HLS startup, SourceLoaded selection briefly changed audio to German, then a native audio-change event restored English before Ready. Reversing the audio/subtitle call order did not prevent this. The app selects once at initial Ready, when initial media is ready, and verifies the intended current Source before selecting. This is an observation of this SDK and fixture, not a promise about every stream.

The test vod-multiaudio fixture has English/German audio metadata and native HLS WebVTT subtitle renditions. These audio labels identify test renditions, not translated soundtracks. Native renditions provide a route shared by iOS and tvOS; external SourceConfig subtitles do not provide the same tvOS System UI route.

blocks.caption: The tvOS configuration form uses remote focus, Select and the system keyboard for initial language preferences.
Fit, Fill (crop) and Stretch are native focusable choices in the tvOS form.

blocks.text: To remove initial track preferences, clear the audio language, choose Automatic subtitles and Apply, or select a source preset. To return scaling to startup behavior, choose Fit and Apply when it differs. Equal video/view aspect ratios can make the scaling choices look identical.
When something does not work

items: If the app builds but cannot play, check the Player license, allowed bundle identifier, network, and reference source. An empty Local.xcconfig used only for compilation does not provide a playback license.
When generating the project for the first time, run sync-env.sh, synchronize the shared UI, then run xcodegen generate.
If the HLS rewind buttons are disabled, start playback first. While paused, the app may continue waiting for the window to become available.
If the paused playback position falls outside the live retention window, the DvrWindowExceeded event requests a return to the live edge.
TimeChanged snapshots also check whether a live stream has ended and become VOD. This handles cases where DurationChanged alone would miss the transition.

blocks.text: To try a progressive MP4, enter a reachable HTTP or HTTPS URL in Configure source and playback, select Progressive MP4, and Apply. The server must support the requests required by the Player, including byte ranges for seeking. Compare playback and seeking with an HLS source.

items.label: Implementation FAQ: configuration and UI issues

blocks.text: Use the SDK default player controls
Default provides normal playback, timeline seeking and the source's track menus. Scroll inside the player menu to reach options below its viewport.

items: On iPhone/iPad select Default; tvOS uses native System UI. Load media with the audio/subtitle tracks you want to compare and start playback. On tvOS use the remote’s Play/Pause command.
Pause, resume and drag the timeline. In Settings, choose a speed preset or an available audio/subtitle track.
Use API inspector → Operations for an arbitrary volume or speed value. Choose Native PlayerView to try fullscreen and view APIs.

blocks.text: Stock speed choices are presets, and its speaker control can toggle mute without a numeric volume slider. These limits describe the default controls only; they do not describe the API inspector's coverage or accepted arguments.

Return to Default on iPhone/iPad after comparing a custom mode. UI changes and the app’s surrounding forms are separate: changing colors, component layout or SwiftUI controls requires the code changes described in the implementation guide.
Run APIs and read their results

The inspector separates Operations, State and Events. Operations invokes an SDK command; State reads current values; Events records notifications. Keep the same source and change one item at a time to connect an action with its result.

items: Open API inspector → Operations, filter Player.volume and choose it. Enter a whole number such as 50 within 0–100 and Run API. Read argument errors. Show operation code displays the Swift call for the current valid arguments.

blocks.caption: Player.volume with an editable numeric argument and Run API. Show operation code displays its Swift call.

items: Switch to State, filter Player.volume and choose Refresh SDK state. Compare the actual value with your command. Refresh after later operations as needed. When finished, use the same operation to restore the previous value.

blocks.caption: The State pane reads Player.volume from the current SDK player after the operation.

items: In Events, clear the old entries and enable recording before the next trial. Use Play/Pause or a supported seek, then inspect event name, owner and SDK timestamp. For asynchronous actions, also check the completion event and resulting position.

Filter by event or owner. Typed listeners and Combine publishers select the subscription method. Registration alone does not mean an event occurred; Player and Source listeners can report the same playback event.

blocks.caption: The tvOS API inspector uses the same Operations, State and Events workflow with remote focus and Select.

blocks.title: Command and completion
blocks.text: A submitted call does not establish receiver playback, a SharePlay participant or active Picture-in-Picture. Inspect state/events and use the required source, host and device. PlayerView operations need the Native PlayerView host described next.
Choose the video presentation

In API inspector, the Player view host section is above the Operations, State and Events panes. Presentation offers SDK SwiftUI, SDK SwiftUI with bindings, Native PlayerView, AVPlayerLayer and AVPlayerViewController. A change recreates the player and reloads the applied source; SDK SwiftUI is the default.

Player factory is a separate choice. The default PlayerFactory attaches Analytics when configured; PlayerCoreFactory and the deprecated PlayerFactory.create path create the player without that wrapper. Changing factories recreates the player. Keep the default when comparing the attached Analytics collector.

rows: SDK SwiftUI with bindings
Change Picture-in-Picture and scaling bindings; inspect availability.
Native PlayerView
Run fullscreen and Picture-in-Picture operations and inspect view events.
AVPlayerLayer
Compare a registered video layer with the separate app controls and scaling.
AVPlayerViewController
Compare AVKit controls and Show AVKit playback controls.

blocks.text: Picture-in-Picture and remote playback require compatible platforms and devices. Read availability state before use. Show presentation code explains how the selected view, layer or controller is registered with the same Bitmovin player.

To return to the default display method, choose SDK SwiftUI. For the configured Analytics collection path, choose PlayerFactory (with configured Analytics) in the separate factory selector. Enabling Picture-in-Picture is separate from availability and active state; check all three before treating it as working.
SharePlay sessions

items: In API inspector → Operations, find SharePlay GroupSession and select Listen for sessions. This receives actual sessions created by the operating system; none is joined automatically.
With a loaded source, Activate current source activity asks the OS to activate its SharePlay activity. It shares the source URL and title, so choose an appropriate source before activation.
Select an actual OS session, then Coordinate current player or Coordinate and join. Participating players need matching SourceConfig.options.sharePlayIdentifier values.
Refresh group state to read the session state and participant count. Leave selected session requests this app's departure; Stop listening only stops observation.

blocks.text: SharePlay requires OS eligibility, an appropriate system session and the Group Activities signing capability. A simulator with no eligible session can still show the controls, but it cannot provide a fabricated GroupSession. Show SharePlay code explains the public coordination call.
Offline HLS on iOS and iPadOS

Use a physical iPhone or iPad to verify downloads and playback from saved media. In the tested SDK 3.128.0 and iOS 27 Simulator environment, initialization and track discovery succeeded, but the media download did not complete. These simulator operations do not verify offline playback.

items: Apply an on-demand HLS source and its DRM settings in the main configuration, then Open offline HLS inspector. Live HLS has no finite download. This panel is unavailable on tvOS.
Set the Wi-Fi restriction and minimum free space. Initialize with SDK defaults or OfflineConfig to save the process-wide startup settings.

After the first setup or a change to initialization options, fully close and reopen the app. The SDK requires initialization during app launch, when the saved settings are applied. Apply the on-demand HLS source and DRM settings again, then reopen the offline inspector.
Select applied HLS source as offline asset. Use an explicit identifier to address that asset again. Fetch available audio and subtitle tracks and choose their download actions.
Choose a download operation and Run offline API. Inspect progress, offlineState and events; track discovery or a submitted call is not download completion.

After completion, choose whether playback must be restricted to cached media, then Create OfflineSourceConfig and Load cached source. Changing the restriction requires creating OfflineSourceConfig again before loading it. It uses the current player; applying the main configuration returns to its remote source.

blocks.caption: The offline inspector lists actual SDK audio/subtitle tracks and their download actions.

blocks.text: Suspend, resume, cancel, delete and offline-license operations affect the selected asset. Delete removes its cached media. FairPlay renewal and synchronization need a suitable license service. Last operation code, SDK state and events distinguish an accepted call from a completed operation.

Refresh offline state reads progress and offlineState. Selecting a different asset removes its UI listener but does not cancel an existing download; use the asset’s suspend or cancel operation to stop it. Delete removes its cached media. Applying or reloading the main configuration returns from cached playback to the remote source.
Google Cast on iOS and iPadOS

items: Open Google Cast inspector. Enter the receiver application ID and optional urn:x-cast:… namespace, then choose background sessions, discovery and receiver-stop behavior.
Choose initializeCasting(options:) and Run Cast API before enabling RemoteControlConfig.isCastEnabled in player settings. Empty receiver fields use SDK defaults.
Initialization is process-wide. Changing initialized options saves them for the next full app launch. Close and reopen the app; recreating a player alone does not replace Cast.
Refresh Cast state to inspect initialization, availability and connection separately. Choose receiver playback or messaging operations and add a listener to observe notifications.

blocks.caption: Receiver and discovery options in the Google Cast inspector. They configure the app process's startup.
The sender is initialized; receiver availability and connection are separate state values.

blocks.title: Receiver requirements
blocks.text: Receiver playback needs a compatible Cast device, local-network permission and suitable media. Custom receivers also need their _APPID._googlecast._tcp entry in Info.plist and a native rebuild; the default service is included. Initialization alone does not establish discovery or receiver playback. Google Cast is not provided by the tvOS sample.

Run remove(listener:) to stop recording Cast notifications. Disable automatic initialization next launch affects the next process startup; it does not uninitialize the current sender. End a receiver session explicitly when needed, considering Stop receiver when ending session. The setup screenshots do not establish receiver discovery or playback.
Applied configuration code

Use Configuration → Show applied code to retain the settings already sent to the SDK. Compare it before and after Apply. The screenshots beside the configuration steps show the iPad and tvOS output. Unapplied edits are excluded and license values are placeholders.

Initial track preferences appear as one-time selection logic. This output is a reference for integration, not a complete independent app. Follow the implementation guide for configuration types, UI changes, callback resources, useful features and Analytics/Observability.
